issue.title: CMAKE parse errors when configuring on Windows x64
issue.body:
Windows 10 Pro x64

Full disclosure, I am a student and new to CMAKE as well as working with third party C++ libraries, so I hope I will have provided enough information here. On my first attempt building from source, I initially ran into an error telling me that openssl "is not compatible with my version of Windows", yet when installing and setting to %path% both the 32 bit version, verifying it works with "openssl -v", then repeating the process with the 64 bit version, I was able to get both running just fine outside of working with this repo. I left the 64 bit version installed and tried again by starting over from the beginning, and now I don't even reach that stage. When trying to build again, I receive the following error message. 

```
CMake Error at liblzma-stamp/download-liblzma.cmake:167:
  Parse error.  Function missing ending ")".  Instead found unterminated
  string with text "

  )

  ".


CMake Error: Error processing file: C:/Users/logst/MAVSDK/build/default/third_party/liblzma/liblzma-prefix/src/liblzma-stamp/download-liblzma.cmake
ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed.
CMake Error at third_party/cmake/build_target.cmake:51 (message):
  C:/Users/logst/MAVSDK/build/default/third_party/liblzma failed to build!
Call Stack (most recent call first):
  third_party/CMakeLists.txt:14 (build_target)


-- Configuring incomplete, errors occurred!
```


I looked in the local repository and could not find the file specified, so I am not sure what else to do here. My whole purpose of building from source was to obtain a .dll file, as while trying to include the Windows x64 release in my current project I kept getting a couple hundred linker errors, one example included below:

```
mavsdk.lib(curl_wrapper.obj) : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol "__declspec(dllimport) public: class std::basic_istream<char,struct std::char_traits<char> > 
```

I have verified that I added the include directory and linked the .lib file appropriately for the environment I am working in, and got stuck there. The __declspec(dllimport) led me to believe that recompiling to add a .dll to the project might fix it, so now I am here.
